Connected frames: overnight results

Author: 1612-engineer 6f54f02c · Issue #1612 · 24 September 2026

1 · The decision

Connected frames do not establish a clear improvement over the selected reader. Keep the selected 2018–2021 parent for the placement experiment.

The best completed context arm trains on 2016–2021. Its held-out loss is 0.820636, compared with 0.825424 for the selected parent. The average loss reduction is +0.004788, with a 95% range of [-0.000132, +0.009736].

Loss measures surprise at the next detector event and its waiting time; lower is better. The parent is the selected 2018–2021 reader with depth and session-clock inputs. An arm is one independent training run with a specified span of years. Held-out means the same 58 trading days in 2022, used for comparison but never for weight updates. A token is one recorded detector fact presented to the model. An update changes the learned weights using one group of observations. A paired range resamples the same whole days for both models; a range wholly above zero supports improvement. The frequency table predicts from the latest event set and recorded depth.

All three required spans have saved results. Time limits prevent a training-convergence or older-year stopping claim. Any time-limited arm is provisional: its selected score is observed evidence, but its training has not passed the original convergence rule. These are development results, not a trading-profit verdict.

2 · What the learning curves establish

An update processes one group of 64 adjacent, nonempty sixteen-bar windows, computes the event and waiting-time losses, and changes the model weights once. Each colored curve shows held-out loss for one training span. Update zero must reproduce the parent before context learning begins.

Every arm starts from the same saved parent and a fresh optimizer. The existing lane, depth, and clock statistics - the means and scales used to normalize numeric inputs - remain fixed. New relationship and market-wide inputs use statistics from that arm’s training years only. For scoring, every arm uses the same fixed 2019–2021 training windows and 2022 comparison windows.

The original stopping rule checks every 800 updates. Once four scheduled checks exist, training stops when the final check does not clearly improve over the first of those four. A time limit can stop a run sooner; that is an operational stop, not evidence of convergence.

Because 2022 chooses checkpoints and training spans, these uncertainty ranges describe development comparisons. They do not turn 2022 into an untouched final test.

3 · Does context resolve the one-bar question?

For the best context arm, one-bar loss is 0.299593, versus 0.322979 for the parent and 0.318026 for the frequency table.

One-bar wait means the next detector event arrives on the next bar. This is the dominant short-wait group that the earlier isolated-frame reader struggled to separate from the frequency table. It is the most direct check of whether connected market structure supplies useful missing information.

Rows report loss within each waiting-time group. Event loss averages the event kinds over tokens with an observed next event; waiting-time loss averages the selected tokens. The overall score uses the original full-sample denominators, so a simple unweighted average of the rows does not reproduce it.

Censored means observation ends before the next event can be labeled. Those examples still contribute the waiting-time survival loss, but have no next-event label. They are kept separate rather than assigned a fabricated arrival.

The table compares the exact same tokens under the selected context checkpoint, the unchanged parent, and the frequency table. Its event and wait totals are checked against the saved evaluation within one millionth.

The best context run lowers one-bar loss, but increases loss for waits of two through ten bars. This is a partial improvement in timing, not a uniform gain. The overall paired comparison remains uncertain.

A gain here supports the usefulness of market context for event prediction. It does not by itself establish better entries, exits, costs, or profitability; the placement experiment must test those outcomes.

4 · What the model can now see

Context is the recorded state of the frame’s connected structures at its event bar. An edge describes why another frame is connected. Globals describe the market at that bar, shared across the roots being scored. A root is the frame whose next event is being predicted.

Previously absent token kindWhere its information enters now
Base meterRecorded base-meter connection, range ratio, origin/pivot positions and ages; market position in globals.
Frame linksAll six recorded link types enter the edge buffer: predecessor, corrected ruler, shared defended pivot, predecessor pivot, standing at admission, crossed destination.
Frame stateActive/ended state, end age, and latest frontier age and position.
Level interaction / level stateTwenty-four level slots carry touch counts, first/last touch ages, latest interaction age and normalized level position. Complete interaction histories are not added as new token kinds.
FrontierLatest captured frontier and its age enter state. This does not substitute the high-water mark for the latest frontier.
Market advanceCurrent market position, range, session and active-structure counts enter globals. No separate market-advance token sequence is introduced.
Leg membershipRecorded membership connection, cursor index when present, and connection age.
Anchor positionSelected and predecessor origin/pivot positions and their ages, expressed for the root.
Measured-move touchNo direct touch token or dedicated touch field enters this change. Detector consequences may affect existing structure; that is not a direct touch input.
Sweep parentRecorded parent connection and age; five captured parent facts when that same-bar sweep snapshot exists, otherwise explicit absence.
Level admissionRecorded level presence and normalized position enter the level slots; no new admission-token sequence.

The model reads connected frame histories, combines them with state and edges through the same relationship architecture used by placement, appends the globals, and uses a projection, a learned linear map, to add that result to each token of the root on that bar. The event and waiting-time heads retain their original loss definitions.

5 · Causality, reproducibility and cost

Each connected set, state and edge comes from the detector’s recorded facts at or before the prediction bar. The history reader includes all same-bar facts under the existing rule and masks later bars. Root-relative coordinates come from captured admission facts. The current range and market position come from that bar’s placement snapshots; missing facts carry explicit presence flags.

The new projection starts at exactly zero. The real-data check compares every saved training and held-out score field and day row against the parent, with tolerance 10−7. Fixtures also check mirrored market structure, exclusion of a connected frame’s next-bar event, and byte-identical rerun and checkpoint/resume.

All learned computation runs in MLX, Apple’s machine-learning runtime, on the GPU, the graphics processor used here for training. Packed connections remove absent slots; shared readouts compute the same frame/bar once. Fixed-order GPU reductions preserve reproducibility. Work scales with actual connected records, rather than a square of all live frames.

Reported update time includes preparation not hidden by prefetch, GPU work, checkpoint saving and cache release. Scoring above includes the initial, scheduled and final checks; the separate waiting-time diagnostic is retained in each arm record. Each completed update has a recoverable checkpoint.

Budget exception: the ticket requested 45 minutes per arm and three hours total. The first implementation forecast 392 minutes per arm. Packing reduced the worst measured update from 46.8 to 4.7 seconds and peak memory from 118 to 52 GB. The exact launch probe forecasts 231.8 minutes per arm at 4.098 seconds/update.

I apply your subsequent overnight instruction as authorization for up to 150 minutes per arm, stopping by 6:30 AM PDT for publication before 7. The original budget miss remains explicit. No histories, training years, loss terms, or validation checks are removed to disguise it.

6 · Recommendation and limits

DecisionRecommendationReason
Placement experiment (#1591)Keep the selected 2018–2021 parent for the placement experiment.The comparison uses the same fixed development population and preserves the parent at update zero.
Medium reader (larger history model)Do not retry the medium reader on this evidence.More capacity would add cost before the missing-information hypothesis is established.
Older training yearsDo not add years before 2016 on this evidence. Resume the existing three spans before drawing an older-year conclusion.All three required spans have saved results. Time limits prevent a training-convergence or older-year stopping claim.
Final trading verdictKeep 2023 outside this development experiment.2022 is reused for checkpoint and span selection; placement needs its own untouched final assessment.

Continuation: preserve the saved state and resume the 2018–2021 comparison first in a separate bounded follow-up. Its one-bar improvement makes completion worth testing; finish the existing three spans before extending the data ladder. No span before 2016 runs overnight, and no arm reaches the original training stopping rule.

The best context artifact is an event-pretraining checkpoint, with reader, depth/clock input, relationship-layer and head weights. Placement must deliberately map those learned modules through its transfer path; simply pointing an older reader-only loader at the file is not a completed transfer.

The full shared detector-history index is opened to perform availability-bounded lookups. The learner materializes no 2023 tokens or targets, and this work performs no 2023 assessment. This distinction matters when interpreting the clean-year boundary.

FAQ — what differs from the original plan?

Why does this run exceed the original timing target? Context requires reading additional connected histories. Removing padded and repeated relationship work fixes a major implementation cost, but does not eliminate that additional reader work. Your overnight instruction supplies the longer bounded window; the report does not claim the original timing gate passed.

Did faster execution change what the model can see? No recorded connection is dropped. The packed GPU implementation matches placement’s forward calculation and gradients in fixtures, including absent-edge cases. Determinism and the zero-start comparison remain gates.

Can these results be read as trading profit? No. They measure prediction of detector events and waits. The next experiment must evaluate placement decisions, execution costs and ambiguity under the existing trading contracts.

Is there a review limitation? The current review has no high-severity findings. Three lower-severity invocation checks are deferred: missing parent, a different input dictionary, and startup with almost no time left. This run supplies the parent, verifies identical pinned dictionaries, and reserves hours for each required span. Those unsupported cases do not affect these results.

Retention

Artifacts live outside the repository. RETENTION.md in the artifact directory defines preservation through 2026-12-31 and while placement depends on the selected checkpoint. Bulk buffers may be removed only after downstream users no longer require them.
